content.overview: BNS s. 10 — Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which. BNS restatement of IPC 72. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 72. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 10 is the rule on “Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which”. The section provides that in all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of which of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 10 exists so that “Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which” has a closed legal test in Chapter II — Of Punishments. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Death, life, imprisonment, forfeiture, fine, and community service. How sentences combine, commute and enhance.

The provision in detail
10. In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of which of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 10 (Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which), Chapter II — Of Punishments.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of which of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 10 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 10 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
